title: Fritz Haber reverse-engineered the Red Pyramid for his ammonia process
summary: Geoffrey Drumm tells of Fritz Haber reverse-engineered the Red Pyramid for his ammonia process, about early 1900s at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And my hypothesis is that old Fritz Habber in the same process that I did in investigating the red pyramid reverse engineered the same mechanisms of operation that drive the system.

And this is the original apparatus
>> that Fritz Habber made.
>> And this is it in comparison to the
three chambers of the Red Pyramid.
tellings.difference: Shows Haber's original apparatus next to the three Red Pyramid chambers but does not mention Bosch.
tellings.link_reason: The same claim that Fritz Haber's ammonia apparatus mirrors the Red Pyramid's chambers, told here as a side-by-side comparison of the two.

as_told.title: Fritz Haber's apparatus compared with the Red Pyramid chambers

plain: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who argues the pyramids were machines, tells podcast host Jesse Michels his idea about Fritz Haber, a German chemist who, with Carl Bosch, worked out a way to make ammonia in the early 1900s. Drumm says Haber studied the Red Pyramid in Egypt, which has three inner chambers, and copied how it worked, pointing to a book that mentions an Egyptian banker funding Haber's project and to postcards Haber dated from Egypt. He sets a picture of Haber's original apparatus beside the pyramid's three chambers to show they match. If true, the pyramid would have been an ancient chemical plant.
